stem: Chitra measures a ribbon on a ruler marked only in centimetres. The cut end sits between the $11\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $12\,\mathrm{cm}$ marks.

parts.text: Which claim correctly states how she should report the length more accurately?

options.text: Report $11\,\mathrm{cm}$, because the cut end has not reached $12\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Split the $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ gap into equal smaller parts and count how many the cut end passes.
Treat the printed $11$ on the ribbon spool as the measured length.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The tip falls between whole-centimetre marks, so the $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ unit interval must be split into equal smaller parts and those parts counted.

teacher.key_rationale: Between whole marks, equal subunit parts of the same centimetre interval give a finer length. Whole-unit only, or a printed spool number, miss that measurement step.
